rooms.title: Atomic Habits
rooms.body:
Atomic Habits argues that small, consistent routines compound into large results over time.

1. What is the "1% better every day" claim?
<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Improving by roughly 1% daily compounds to about 37x over a year.
</details>

rooms.body: The book behind the [[Atomic Habits]] concept note.

rooms.title: book - deep work

rooms.body: One note per day, for capture. Rolls up into the [[Weekly Review]].

rooms.body:
Root-level overview note. There is a second, deliberately homonymous "Overview" note under
projects/ — used to exercise the shortest-unique-path wikilink resolution rule.

rooms.title: reading list
rooms.body: Currently reading: [[Book - Deep Work]] and [[Book - Atomic Habits]].

rooms.title: second brain
rooms.body:
A "second brain" is an external system for capturing and connecting what you learn, so
recall does not depend on unaided memory.

- [[Zettelkasten]] - the atomic-note method this system is built on
- [[Spaced Repetition]] - how retention is maintained over time

rooms.title: spaced repetition
rooms.body:
Spaced repetition schedules review just before you would otherwise forget, using a
forgetting-curve model. Tagged #srs for quick filtering.

rooms.title: weekly review
rooms.body:
A weekly pass back over [[Daily Notes]] and the [[Reading List]].

This note also links to the ambiguous [[Notes]] target on purpose, to exercise the
duplicate-basename-at-equal-depth case.

rooms.title: welcome
rooms.body:
Welcome to this vault. Start with [[Second Brain]], then branch into [[Zettelkasten#Origins]]
and [[Daily Notes]]. See also the vault [[Overview]] (deliberately homonymous with
projects/Overview.md — the root note, being fewer path segments away, should win).

This vault also references a note that was deliberately removed from the corpus: [[Leaked]].

rooms.title: zettelkasten
rooms.body:
The Zettelkasten method links small, atomic notes to each other rather than filing them into
a fixed hierarchy.

See also [[Second Brain]] and [[Atomic Habits|the habits book]] for an applied example.
